title: Normalized scalar extension at the positive finite root levels
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite intermediate extension of Q_l in its fixed algebraic closure, and X any scheme. Set a0=coefficientMap(integralMap(l,bottomField(l)),X) and a=coefficientMap(integralMap(l,E),X), using [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-maps]. There is a natural isomorphism from spIntegralTwistSystem(X,l,bottomField(l)) followed by restriction along a0 and extension along a to spIntegralTwistSystem(X,l,E), using the positive-level towers of [sk-def-sp-tate-twist]. At each n >= 0, its hom after the ordinary scalar unit is spEllMap(X,l,bottom<=E,n) tensor the identity of mu_(l^(n+1),X). This asserts only the finite-level tensor calculation and compatibility with the coefficient-reduction/root-power transitions. It asserts no inverse-limit, flatness, derived, or diagonal comparison. No invertibility or Noetherian hypothesis on X is needed.

source.place: paragraph (1), finite-level scalar extension of the root tower; sec-proetale-coefficients/sk-def-sp-tate-twist/_section.md, finite-level tensor formulas

proof.text: For N=l^(n+1), the actual condensed reduction p_E:O_E -> O_E/(N) is the cokernel of N times the identity. Check this on every profinite test S. A continuous quotient-valued function lifts continuously by choosing representatives of the discrete quotient. A continuous function in the kernel divides by N continuously: multiplication by l^(n+1) on O_E is an embedding (the proved PadicAlgCl.isEmbedding_natCast_pow_mul in WeilConjectures.NumberTheory.Padics.IntegersModPow), its range is the kernel ideal (PadicAlgCl.exists_natCast_pow_mul_eq), and the inverse of an embedding is continuous on its range. This gives an exact sequence of abelian groups on each test. Apply the proved source-library sectionwise cokernel criterion CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isColimitCokernelCoforkOfSurjective (WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.Adic.ZModPowCokernel) to obtain the asserted cokernel in condensed abelian sheaves.

Pullback from the point is a left adjoint and preserves this cokernel. Tensoring on the right with mu_N also preserves it. The map N times the identity becomes zero, since N annihilates mu_N; hence the resulting reduction tensor identity is an isomorphism. The linear free-module map from O_E tensor_Z mu_N to the actual finite twist has this underlying map, so it too is an isomorphism, as forgetting the module action reflects isomorphisms.

The bottom integral coefficient map is an isomorphism by its pointwise normalization in the base coefficient identification. Its tensor with the roots, followed by the bottom reduction map of step 2, gives an isomorphism from the free Z_l module on mu_N to the restricted bottom finite twist. Extension of scalars carries the free Z_l module on mu_N to the free O_E module on mu_N: compose the free/forget and extend/restrict adjunctions and use uniqueness of left adjoints. Compose the inverse of the extended bottom comparison, this free-module scalar isomorphism, and the target reduction comparison. This is the required O_E-linear level isomorphism.

The unit equation for uniqueness of left adjoints fixes the free scalar isomorphism on roots; naturality of the ordinary extension unit and the defining quotient square of spEllMap then give the requested normalization. For successive indices, the spEllMap reduction squares commute by cancelling the epic integral reduction. Tensor with the root transition to obtain the finite-level square. The extension-unit Hom equivalence is injective, so this square and the level normalization give naturality of the linear level isomorphisms. NatTrans.ofOpSequence assembles them, and pointwise invertibility gives the tower isomorphism. These constructions use no invertibility of l, root generator, nonempty-scheme assumption, or inverse limit.

lean.statement:
theorem diagonalIntegral_rootLevelScalars (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField l) (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    ∃ i : (spIntegralTwistSystem X l (bottomField l) ⋙
        Mod.comap (coefficientMap (integralMap l (bottomField l)) X)) ⋙
          Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap (integralMap l E) X) ≅
        spIntegralTwistSystem X l E,
      ∀ n : ℕ,
        Mod.extendUnitHom (coefficientMap (integralMap l E) X)
            ((Mod.comap (coefficientMap (integralMap l (bottomField l)) X)).obj
              (spIntegralTwistLevel X l (bottomField l) n)) ≫
          (i.hom.app (op n)).hom =
        spEllMap X l (show (bottomField l).1 ≤ E.1 from bot_le) n ⊗ₘ
          𝟙 (Scheme.proEtaleRootsOfUnitySheaf X (l ^ (n + 1)))
